REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP)
Request for Proposal Information:

Proposals Due: 4:00 p.m. on April 10, 2025

RFP Title: Information Technology Strategic
Plan

Proposals shall be submitted electronically to
the following email address:

Date Issued: March 19, 2025

leong@snohomishwa.gov

Contact:

leong@snohomishwa.gov

INTRODUCTION
The City of Snohomish is soliciting proposals from qualified consultant firms to develop a Six-Year
Information Technology Strategic Plan.

A copy of this Request for Proposal (RFP) and City’s
Professional Services Agreement may be obtained from City’s web site at
https://snohomishwa.gov/105/Bids-RFPs-RFQs.

The successful consultant(s) will be required to
sign the City’s Professional Services Agreement.

The City will not sign any company’s service
agreement, contract, or other form of agreement.

The City of Snohomish reserves the right to reject any and all proposals and to waive irregularities
and informalities in the submittal and evaluation process.

This RFP does not obligate the City to
pay any costs incurred by respondents in the preparation and submission of a proposal.

Furthermore, the RFP does not obligate the City to accept or contract for any expressed or implied
services.

The City requires that no person shall, on the grounds of race, religion, color, national origin, sex,
age, marital status, political affiliation, sexual orientation, or the presence of any sensory, mental,
or physical disability be excluded from participation in, be denied the benefits of,

or be otherwise
subjected to discrimination under any program or activity.

The City of Snohomish further assures
that every effort will be made to ensure non-discrimination in all of its programs and activities,
whether those programs are federally funded or not.

In addition to nondiscrimination compliance requirements, a Service Provider ultimately awarded a
contract shall comply with federal, state and local laws, statutes and ordinances relative to the
execution of the work.

This requirement includes, but is not limited to, protection of public and
employee safety and health;
disabilities;
environmental protection;
waste reduction and recycling;
the protection of natural resources;
permits;
fees;
taxes;
and similar subjects.

ABOUT THE CITY OF SNOHOMISH
The IT Department supports and manages the city’s entire IT infrastructure from hardware to
software applications, LAN and WAN communications, telephony hardware and software, end
user desktop support,

other IT related equipment, and communications tools including City
website and social media.
The IT Department supports around 100 systems and 60 users.

The IT Department currently
supports all IT related functions at the City except for the management of GIS software and Utilities
(SCADA) system.

The City’s expanding GIS service and one GIS staff member is under the
Planning Department.

The City expects the selected consultant to incorporate all software and IT
functions in their analysis, regardless of which department currently has oversight or primary
responsibility.

OBJECTIVE
Assess, evaluate, and develop recommendations for a six-year strategic plan that incorporates the
City’s IT needs, including work, staffing,

and budget required to support:
 Existing IT capabilities,

infrastructure and programs
 City’s comprehensive plan
 Council-approved goals and budgets
 New Civic Campus technology planning
 Stated and approved department objectives
 Ability to connect systems
 Ability to consolidate systems
 Increase technology in the field
 Evaluate IT staff FTE versus consultant

services (staffing needs)
 Simplify IT processes
 Data center equipment requirements
 Cloud versus on premise servers
 Centralized versus decentralized decision making and procurement of all technology
related hardware, software,

and support services
 Analysis of existing software footprint and recommendations on procurement strategies for
cost reduction
 Reduce paper use and storage
 GIS management
 Social media/website interaction (i.e.

single input of information)
 Surveillance infrastructure
 IT responsibilities in relation to other departments

REQUESTED SERVICES
Services include any tasks necessary to produce the requested deliverables.

Specific areas of
interest include (but are not necessarily limited to) the following:


Assessment of customer satisfaction, to include interviews with a wide range of City staff.

Assessment of effective use of technology resources and staff access to technology
services.
Evaluation of current organizational structure and governance practices.
A capability/maturity assessment for processes and skills.

This should include
recommendations for how to be more productive with the resources that we have and
ensure alignment of IT capabilities (people, skill sets, process, and technology) with the
needs of City operations.

Evaluation of moving to Cloud based technologies, support for mobile computing options,
user-experience and usability strategies, storage and backup strategies, and skill levels
related to the technologies needed now and needed over the next six years (infrastructure
assessment and roadmap).
Technology needs and services planning for the new Civic Campus.
Assessment of the City’s current GIS program and opportunities for future expansion.

Analysis of our current technology stack for network, storage, backup, database, desktop,
mobile, reporting, data analytics, and communications.

Identification of opportunities for significant improvements in IT operations and for new
ways that IT can add substantial value to the City.
Assessment of IT security and protocols.

Recommendations for management of legacy applications & systems, and transition of
legacy application data to a modern platform for better management and records retention.

DELIVERABLES
Deliverables will include (but may not be limited to):
 A six-year IT strategic plan with capital and operating funding estimates.
 A three-year tactical plan, with the 2026 plan aligned with the adopted budget and a 20272028 plan that includes associated funding needs.

 Strength, weaknesses, and risk analysis
 A list of opportunities for improvement
 Create, deploy, and analyze a user survey

well as options, if any, for changes in staffing levels and/or organization structure.

Recommendations and a high-level roadmap on high-level technology areas including
cloud strategy and infrastructure as a service, data analytics, storage technology,
document management and retention, and any other identified by the consultant.
A final document suitable for posting on the Internet, including a Microsoft Word version.
At least two presentations (one to IT Steering and one to the City Council).

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS
We are looking for a consultant (or team) that:
 Has significant experience with municipal technology strategic plans in similar-sized cities.

 All IT personnel having direct access to confidential information shall have a Washington
State and national fingerprint-based background check and completed the technical
security awareness training.

A re-background (criminal history) check should be conducted
every five years.

 Has deep technical experience to create tactical plans and to cost projects at a detailed
level in the following areas:

o Project costing and organizational structure
o Security
o Civic campus and public facility technology designs
o GIS
o Commonly used municipal COTS application systems including supporting
interfaces between best-of-breed systems
o Storage, backup,

and disaster recovery & continuity

SELECTION PROCESS
The City will evaluate the Proposals and conduct interviews with the selected finalists.

The final
selection, if any, will be the consultant(s) which, in the opinion of the City, best meets the
requirements set forth in this RFP and is in the best interest of the City.

Proposals will be evaluated based on:
 Company Background & References – 15%
 Relevant Experience & Qualifications – 30%
 Project Approach – 20%
 Budget & Value – 25%
 Quality, Clarity & Completeness – 10%
